policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV's 'what mean ye' directly renders the qere as a question addressed to the plural 'you,' distinguishing מַה לָּכֶם from the ketiv מלכם.

ASV's 'outstretched' expresses the shared lexical sense and does not distinguish the qere נְטוּי֣וֹת from the ketiv נטוות; no mapped textual note decides between them, so the base fallback is retained.
